target: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v5.xlsx

rows.Detail: The Kafka host, topic naming, ACL model and schema registry are confirmed in Wave 0. The outbox and the Azure Event Hubs fallback are kept until the topics exist.

Architecture v5 decision 1 is closed in Wave 0. The answer names the cluster that hosts the 19 service topics and rwb.decision-record.v1, its capacity and retention, the team that runs it, the ACL model and the trigger for the Event Hubs fallback, and is recorded in this document and in the Environment and Deployment Design. Cluster name, capacity, running team and fallback trigger: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2014). Ownership and sizing are confirmed in the verification loop.
rows.Basis: GAP-2014; GAP-3248; Arch v5 slides 9 and 39

rows.Detail: The JSON Schema of each event payload is published in the registry and copied into the AsyncAPI documents, or it is confirmed that field names only are the agreed contract for the first release, so that each producer owns its schema types in its CON story. Property types, formats and required flags: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0096).

rows.Rule: Payload of the 15 catalogue-only event types
rows.Detail: The payload of ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished, FileDelivered, FileFailed, RouteDecided, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled, LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, AssetSold, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged is fixed in the CON story of the owning service, with IDs and codes only and no personal data. The schema is registered before the first consumer is built.

The plus rows of Architecture v5 slide 43 are numbered EV-31 to EV-42 on the Events v5 sheet; this replaces their unnumbered state. ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished and LawsuitFiled are not plus rows and stay unnumbered. The missing AsyncAPI operations (ReportPublished, LawsuitFiled, ApprovalDecided and the two guarantee claim events) are added to the AsyncAPI documents of the owning services.
